name: Birt-Hogg-Dubé Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple fibrofolliculomas confirmed by histopathology
Multiple bilateral lung cysts identified on chest imaging
Renal tumors, particularly chromophobe renal carcinoma or oncocytoma
First-degree relative with confirmed Birt-Hogg-Dubé Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria or one major plus one minor criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for FLCN mutation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Typically appear as dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face, neck, and upper torso
Cysts predominantly located in the lower medial and subpleural regions of the lungs
Often multifocal and bilateral, with increased risk of malignancy

common.notes: Recurrent episodes due to rupture of lung cysts
Benign hair follicle tumors similar to fibrofolliculomas
Non-specific symptom possibly related to chronic disease burden

occasional.notes: Shortness of breath related to lung cysts or pneumothorax
May be secondary to renal tumors or cysts

rare.notes: Rare complication of lung cyst rupture

imaging: High-resolution CT scan showing multiple bilateral lung cysts
Abdominal ultrasound or CT revealing renal tumors
genetic: Germline mutation in the FLCN gene (folliculin)
other: Family history of Birt-Hogg-Dubé Syndrome or related symptoms

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cortical tubers and subependymal nodules on brain imaging
Predominantly affects women of childbearing age
Diffuse cystic lung disease without skin lesions
Associated with tuberous sclerosis complex in some cases

references: Schmidt LS, Linehan WM. Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome. GeneReviews. 2020.
Nickerson ML, et al. Mutations in a novel gene lead to kidney tumors, lung wall defects, and benign tumors of the hair follicle in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome. Cancer Cell. 2002.
Toro JR, et al. Lung cysts, spontaneous pneumothorax, and genetic associations in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2007.
